split_policy.primary_axis: tooling/e2e developer-tooling behavior before fixture directory label, formatter source pair, JSON owner contract, tmp report path, script anchor, native code path reference, hosted LLVM probe label, language-server capability label, old-mode label, shim label, fallback label, compatibility label, or migration label
split_policy.positive_rule: developer-tooling positives are limited to hand-authored contracts and formatter fixture sources owned by parser or e2e/tooling; parser may own formatter source syntax, while sema, lowering, IR, and runtime positives must point back to canonical compiler behavior owners
split_policy.canonical_rejection_rule: unpublished language-server capabilities, local-only hosted proof, clang-only hosted execution, source-map/statement-stepping overclaims, wrapper-only action capability, editor-only shadow parser claims, generated-only rows, report-only rows, migration-only rows, old-mode rows, shim rows, fallback rows, and compatibility rows are non-positive rejection or provenance evidence
split_policy.strict_error_rule: hosted LLVM claims without hosted object emission, unowned language-server support claims, wrapper-only action capability, source-map stepping claims without emitted metadata, and report/generated rows promoted as support own fail-closed strict-error evidence
split_policy.provenance_rule: JSON owner contracts, tmp report paths, script anchors, native path references, public action names, schema paths, manifest field names, source fixture paths, debug/source-map labels, hosted probe labels, unsupported capability labels, and formatted source fixture pairs remain provenance unless an owner split claims the behavior boundary
split_policy.retired_surface_rule: old-mode developer tooling, compatibility developer tooling, shim developer tooling, fallback developer tooling, generated-only tooling, report-only tooling, migration-only tooling, wrapper-only tooling, local-only hosted proof, runner-only success, workflow-label-only success, and generated/report rows promoted as support are canonical rejection, strict-error, absent-support, or provenance-only evidence
